images.title: Four take aways, one rule
images.purpose: Set up the four take aways and show the method cue: before taking away, the two fractions must count in the same unit, as the strips for 5/6 and 4/9 show.
images.composition: A column of four short question lines on the left with wide spacing, two garland strips of the same length on the right beside the third line, and one rule line centred at the bottom.
images.exact_structure: Left: 4 question lines stacked with equal spacing; the third line has a reddish purple #CC79A7 rounded box around it. Right, level with the boxed line: two flat jasmine garland strips of exactly the same length, left edges lined up, one above the other. Top strip: cut into 6 equal parts, the 5 leftmost filled teal #0072B2. Bottom strip: cut into 9 equal parts, the 4 leftmost filled amber #E69F00. The part edges do not line up, showing different units. Bottom, centred: one rule line. Exactly 4 question lines, 2 strips, 5 teal parts, 4 amber parts.
labels: make the units the same first

images.takeaway: Make the units the same, then take away.
images.description: Four take away questions listed, with 5/6 − 4/9 boxed beside two equal strips cut into sixths and ninths whose parts do not line up; the rule line says to make the units the same first. No answers are shown.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the strips and say why sixths and ninths cannot be taken from each other yet.

image_decisions.why: Strips in sixths and ninths that do not line up show why a common unit is needed, without giving any answer.
